about:
Panah Project was founded in 2019 in Brooklyn, New York, by husband-and-wife team Morteza Saifi and Evgeniya Khromina. The studio's roots trace back to Nairobi, Kenya, where the pair launched an ethical manufacturing initiative that trained women in local communities to produce luxury-quality garments for international markets, creating more than 50 full-time jobs over five years.

Operating from a single facility at 254 36th Street, the company functions as a design studio and full-service sample factory. Its in-house team handles pattern making, sample making, fabric and trim sourcing, cut-and-sew production, grading, fitting, and draping. The factory focuses on low-minimum-order production for emerging and sustainable brands, while also developing footwear lines through established manufacturing relationships in Europe, Asia, and South America.

Panah Project serves a range of clients including established apparel brands, emerging designers, startups, film and theater productions, footwear labels, and bespoke clients seeking one-of-a-kind pieces such as red-carpet looks. For film and theater, the studio creates bespoke costumes tailored to actor measurements and production timelines; for footwear, it supports development across all major categories with flexible minimums.

The founders cite their Nairobi experience as the foundation for the studio's values—fair wages, long-term opportunity, and craftsmanship. Morteza Saifi, formerly Executive Creative Director at Camuto Group, leads creative and technical direction, while Evgeniya Khromina guides strategy and operations. The company emphasizes a streamlined, under-one-roof process that maintains quality control from design through to market-ready pieces.
